claim: The V409 residue of TUBA1A is located in helix 11' of α-tubulin, near the intradimer interface on the cytoplasmic surface of the microtubule.
source: The V409 residue of TUBA1A is located in helix 11' of α-tubulin, near the intradimer interface on the cytoplasmic surface of the microtubule (Alushin et al., 2014; PDB: 3J6F; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim cites a published structure (PDB: 3J6F) and references Alushin et al., 2014, providing citation-based support for the structural location of the residue.

claim: TUBA1A-V409I and -V409A mutants incorporate into microtubules similar to WT controls.
source: Both the TUBA1A-V409I and -V409A mutants incorporate into microtubules, similar to WT controls, as indicated by the microtubule filaments that can be resolved in the soma (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1A demonstrating microtubule filaments in the soma of neurons expressing the mutants.

claim: TUBA1A-T349E mutant does not assemble into polymer.
source: As a positive control, we expressed the TUBA1A-T349E mutant that does not assemble into polymer, as evidenced by the lack of labeled polymer in the soma (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data in Figure 1A showing lack of polymer in cells expressing T349E mutant.

claim: The amount of 6X-His signal retained after soluble protein extraction is similar between WT- and V409I/A-expressing cells.
source: We find that the amount of 6X-His signal retained after soluble protein extraction is similar between WT- and V409I/A-expressing cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1B measuring 6X-His fluorescence intensity.

claim: TUBA1A-V409I/A mutants assemble similar levels of ectopically expressed tubulin into microtubule polymer as compared to WT.
source: These results suggest that the TUBA1A-V409I/A mutants assemble similar levels of ectopically expressed tubulin into microtubule polymer as compared to WT.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the similar 6X-His signal data presented in Figure 1B.

claim: The majority of GFP+ neurons ectopically expressing TUBA1A-WT successfully migrate from the ventricular zone to the upper cortical plate by E18.5.
source: The majority of GFP + neurons ectopically expressing TUBA1A-WT successfully migrate from the ventricular zone to the upper cortical plate by E18.5 (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by in utero electroporation data shown in Figure 1C demonstrating GFP+ cell distribution in brain sections.

claim: Neurons ectopically expressing TUBA1A-V409I do not migrate to the upper cortical plate as robustly as WT control cells by E18.5.
source: In contrast, neurons ectopically expressing TUBA1A-V409I do not migrate to the upper cortical plate as robustly as WT control cells by E18.5, as evidenced by many neurons remaining in the ventricular, subventricular, and intermediate zones.
evidence: The claim is supported by the distribution of GFP+ cells in brain sections shown in Figure 1C and quantified in Figure 1E.

claim: A majority of TUBA1A-V409A-expressing neurons fail to migrate at all by E18.5 and remain primarily in the ventricular and subventricular zones.
source: Strikingly, a majority of TUBA1A-V409A-expressing neurons fail to migrate at all by E18.5 and remain primarily in the ventricular and subventricular zones.
evidence: The claim is supported by the distribution of GFP+ cells in brain sections shown in Figure 1C and quantified in Figure 1E.

claim: The largest proportion of TUBA1A-WT-expressing cells (43.4%) are found in the upper cortical plate region.
source: We find that the largest proportion of TUBA1A-WT-expressing cells (43.4%) are found in the upper cortical plate region (labeled in orange), while the largest proportion of TUBA1A-V409I-expressing cells (45.4%) are in the intermediate zone and lower cortical plate, and the largest proportion of TUBA1A-V409A-expressing cells (49.4%) are in the ventricular/subventricular zones (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of GFP fluorescence intensity in different cortical zones shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The largest proportion of TUBA1A-V409I-expressing cells (45.4%) are in the intermediate zone and lower cortical plate.
source: We find that the largest proportion of TUBA1A-WT-expressing cells (43.4%) are found in the upper cortical plate region (labeled in orange), while the largest proportion of TUBA1A-V409I-expressing cells (45.4%) are in the intermediate zone and lower cortical plate, and the largest proportion of TUBA1A-V409A-expressing cells (49.4%) are in the ventricular/subventricular zones (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of GFP fluorescence intensity in different cortical zones shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The largest proportion of TUBA1A-V409A-expressing cells (49.4%) are in the ventricular/subventricular zones.
source: We find that the largest proportion of TUBA1A-WT-expressing cells (43.4%) are found in the upper cortical plate region (labeled in orange), while the largest proportion of TUBA1A-V409I-expressing cells (45.4%) are in the intermediate zone and lower cortical plate, and the largest proportion of TUBA1A-V409A-expressing cells (49.4%) are in the ventricular/subventricular zones (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of GFP fluorescence intensity in different cortical zones shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Untransfected control cells successfully reach the cortical plate in all experiments.
source: In each of our experiments, untransfected control cells successfully reach the cortical plate, as evidenced by abundant DAPI signal in the upper cortical plate segment, indicating that the radial glia cells that support migration are not impaired by the transfection of mutant TUBA1A in our experiments.
evidence: The claim is supported by DAPI staining data shown in Figure 1C indicating normal cell distribution in untransfected cells.

claim: TUBA1A-V409I/A mutants act dominantly to disrupt neuron migration.
source: These results suggest that the TUBA1A-V409I/A mutants act dominantly to disrupt neuron migration, with TUBA1A-V409A being more severe than the TUBA1A-V409I mutant.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the migration defects observed in heterozygous expression experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: TUBA1A-V409A is more severe than the TUBA1A-V409I mutant in disrupting neuron migration.
source: These results suggest that the TUBA1A-V409I/A mutants act dominantly to disrupt neuron migration, with TUBA1A-V409A being more severe than the TUBA1A-V409I mutant.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the migration defects of V409I and V409A shown in Figure 1C-E.

claim: TUBA1A-WT-expressing cells in the intermediate and ventricular zones exhibit a clear bipolar morphology.
source: We find that the TUBA1A-WT-expressing cells in the intermediate and ventricular zones exhibit a clear bipolar morphology (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by high-resolution confocal microscopy images shown in Figure 1F.

claim: TUBA1A-V409I-expressing cells in the intermediate and ventricular zones show a primarily bipolar morphology.
source: TUBA1A-V409I-expressing cells in the intermediate and ventricular zones also show a primarily bipolar morphology, however it is again evident that there are more TUBA1A-V409I-expressing cells in these regions as compared to WT-expressing cells (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by high-resolution confocal microscopy images shown in Figure 1F.

claim: TUBA1A-V409A-expressing cells in the intermediate and ventricular zones have elaborate multipolar morphologies with many processes and branches.
source: Most strikingly, the TUBA1A-V409A-expressing cells in the intermediate and ventricular zones have elaborate multipolar morphologies with many processes and branches (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by high-resolution confocal microscopy images shown in Figure 1F.

claim: TUBA1A-V409A-expressing cells exhibit severe migration defects accompanied by morphological defects.
source: We conclude that TUBA1A-V409A-expressing cells exhibit severe migration defects accompanied by morphological defects, while TUBA1A-V409I-expressing cells exhibit intermediate migration defects without a strong morphological phenotype.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the migration and morphology data shown in Figure 1.

claim: TUBA1A-V409I-expressing cells exhibit intermediate migration defects without a strong morphological phenotype.
source: We conclude that TUBA1A-V409A-expressing cells exhibit severe migration defects accompanied by morphological defects, while TUBA1A-V409I-expressing cells exhibit intermediate migration defects without a strong morphological phenotype.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the migration and morphology data shown in Figure 1.

claim: There is no appreciable difference in the number of neurites quantified in stage 2 cells expressing WT or V409I/A mutant TUBA1A.
source: On average, there is no appreciable difference in the number of neurites quantified in stage 2 cells expressing WT or V409I/A mutant TUBA1A.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Most stage 2 neurons have four primary neurites, and secondary or tertiary branches are rarely observed.
source: Most neurons at stage 2 have four primary neurites, and we rarely observe secondary or tertiary branches (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Stage 3 WT and V409I/A mutant neurons have a similar number of primary neurites (5.1±0.4, 4.9±0.4, 5.4±0.4 for WT, V409I, and V409A, respectively).
source: Consistent with this finding, stage 3 WT and V409I/A mutant neurons have a similar number of primary neurites (5.1±0.4, 4.9±0.4, 5.4±0.4 for WT, V409I, and V409A, respectively; Figure 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: TUBA1A-V409I-expressing cells exhibit a slight, but measurable increase in secondary branches as compared to WT cells (0.6±0.2, 0.9±0.3 branches/cell for WT and V409I, respectively).
source: However, TUBA1A-V409I-expressing cells exhibit a slight, but measurable increase in secondary branches as compared to WT cells (0.6±0.2, 0.9±0.3 branches/cell for WT and V409I, respectively; Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: TUBA1A-V409A-expressing cells have a significantly greater number of secondary branches (0.6±0.2, 2.2±0.7 branches/cell for WT and V409A, respectively).
source: Strikingly, TUBA1A-V409A-expressing cells have a significantly greater number of secondary branches, and some also exhibit tertiary branches (secondary: 0.6±0.2, 2.2±0.7 branches/cell, tertiary: 0.01±0.03, 0.3±0.2 branches/cell for WT and V409A, respectively; Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Some TUBA1A-V409A-expressing cells exhibit tertiary branches (0.01±0.03, 0.3±0.2 branches/cell for WT and V409A, respectively).
source: Strikingly, TUBA1A-V409A-expressing cells have a significantly greater number of secondary branches, and some also exhibit tertiary branches (secondary: 0.6±0.2, 2.2±0.7 branches/cell, tertiary: 0.01±0.03, 0.3±0.2 branches/cell for WT and V409A, respectively; Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Neurite growth rates and retraction rates are similar between TUBA1A-WT-, -V409I-, and -V409A-expressing cells.
source: We find that neurite growth rates and retraction rates are similar between TUBA1A-WT-, -V409I-, and -V409A-expressing cells (Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Table 1.

claim: The duration of growth and retraction events is not significantly different between WT and V409I/A mutants.
source: The duration of growth and retraction events is also not significantly different; however, neurites in V409I-expressing cells, and more strikingly V409A, have a lower proportion of retraction events per neurite as compared to WT (34.6%, 25.4%, and 16.6% for WT, V409I, and V409A, respectively; Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Table 1.

claim: Neurites in V409I-expressing cells, and more strikingly V409A, have a lower proportion of retraction events per neurite as compared to WT (34.6%, 25.4%, and 16.6% for WT, V409I, and V409A, respectively).
source: The duration of growth and retraction events is also not significantly different; however, neurites in V409I-expressing cells, and more strikingly V409A, have a lower proportion of retraction events per neurite as compared to WT (34.6%, 25.4%, and 16.6% for WT, V409I, and V409A, respectively; Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Neurites in both V409I and V409A mutants commonly exhibit a paused state, where they are neither growing nor shrinking.
source: In addition, neurites in both mutants commonly exhibit a paused state, where they are neither growing nor shrinking.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 2D and 2E.

claim: Both the proportion of paused events and the duration of these pauses are significantly increased in V409I/A mutants (proportions: 24.0%, 35.6%, and 42.3%, duration: 0.7, 1.2, and 1.4 min for WT, V409I, and V409A, respectively).
source: Both the proportion of paused events and the duration of these pauses are significantly increased in V409I/A mutants (proportions: 24.0%, 35.6%, and 42.3%, duration: 0.7, 1.2, and 1.4 min for WT, V409I, and V409A, respectively; Figure 2D and E; Figure 2—figure supplement 1C; Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 2D, 2E, and Table 1.

claim: The increased branching observed in V409I/A neurons is not due to an increase in neurite growth events or rate.
source: These data suggest that the increased branching observed in V409I/A neurons is not due to an increase in neurite growth events or rate.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the neurite dynamics data showing similar growth rates but fewer retraction events.

claim: V409I/A cells have fewer retraction events and spend an increased amount of time neither growing nor shrinking.
source: Rather, our data supports the hypothesis that V409I/A cells have fewer retraction events and spend an increased amount of time neither growing nor shrinking.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the neurite dynamics data shown in Figure 2D and 2E.

claim: After 4 hr at 4°C, the average number of neurites in TUBA1A-WT-expressing cells is decreased from 4 to 1.5.
source: After 4 hr at 4° C, the average number of neurites in TUBA1A-WT-expressing cells (identified by cytoplasmic GFP displayed in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C) is decreased from 4 to 1.5.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: The remaining neurites in WT cells after 4 hr at 4°C are depleted for β-II tubulin signal and nearly all have retraction bulbs.
source: The remaining neurites are depleted for β-II tubulin signal and nearly all have the retraction bulbs that are characteristic of retracting neurites (Figure 2F–H and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D-F).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2F-H.

claim: By 6 hr at 4°C, the number of neurites per cell is further diminished and β-II tubulin signal is only found in the cell soma of neurons expressing TUBA1A-WT.
source: By 6 hr at 4°C, the number of neurites per cell is further diminished and β-II tubulin signal is only found in the cell soma of neurons expressing TUBA1A-WT (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Neurite loss and the accumulation of retraction bulbs is more gradual in TUBA1A-V409I-expressing cells compared to WT.
source: In contrast to WT controls, neurite loss and the accumulation of retraction bulbs is more gradual in TUBA1A-V409I-expressing cells (Figure 2F–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 2F-G.

claim: TUBA1A-V409A-expressing cells maintain neurites containing robust β-II tubulin signal throughout the cold shock time course, and retraction bulbs begin to form only after 6 hr at 4°C.
source: The most severe effect is detected in TUBA1A-V409A-expressing cells where neurites containing robust β-II tubulin signal are maintained throughout the time course, and retraction bulbs begin to form only after 6 hr at 4°C (Figure 2G–H).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 2G-H.

claim: Expression of TUBA1A-V409I or -V409A creates hyper-stable microtubules in neurites that decrease neurite retraction events and lead to excessive branching.
source: Together, these data suggest that expression of TUBA1A-V409I or -V409A creates hyper-stable microtubules in neurites that decrease neurite retraction events and lead to excessive branching.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cold shock resistance and branching data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Stage 3 control cells ectopically expressing TUBA1A-WT have acetylated tubulin localized primarily to the axon and tyrosinated tubulin throughout the neuron.
source: As expected, stage 3 control cells ectopically expressing TUBA1A-WT have acetylated tubulin localized primarily to the axon and tyrosinated tubulin throughout the neuron (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: TUBA1A-WT cells have the characteristic peak of tyrosinated tubulin at the distal tip of the axon, followed by a sharp increase in acetylated tubulin in the more proximal regions of the process.
source: Additionally, TUBA1A-WT cells have the characteristic peak of tyrosinated tubulin at the distal tip of the axon, followed by a sharp increase in acetylated tubulin in the more proximal regions of the process (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by line scan data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Both TUBA1A-V409I- and -V409A-expressing neurons exhibit tyrosinated tubulin throughout the neuron, similar to that observed in control cells expressing TUBA1A-WT.
source: Both TUBA1A-V409I- and -V409A-expressing neurons also exhibit tyrosinated tubulin throughout the neuron, similar to that observed in control cells expressing TUBA1A-WT (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B-D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: TUBA1A-V409I-expressing cells have a modest, yet statistically insignificant increase in microtubule acetylation at the distal axon tip.
source: TUBA1A-V409I-expressing cells have a modest, yet statistically insignificant increase in microtubule acetylation at the distal axon tip, and a significant increase in microtubule acetylation in the region more proximal to the soma (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: TUBA1A-V409I-expressing cells have a significant increase in microtubule acetylation in the region more proximal to the soma.
source: TUBA1A-V409I-expressing cells have a modest, yet statistically insignificant increase in microtubule acetylation at the distal axon tip, and a significant increase in microtubule acetylation in the region more proximal to the soma (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: TUBA1A-V409A cells exhibit a striking increase in microtubule acetylation at the distal axon tip, as well as in the more proximal region of the process (first 10 µm from distal tip: 1.238±0.303, 1.801±0.372, 2.331±0.596 AU; second 10 µm: 2.442±0.416, 3.505±0.556, 3.868±0.702 AU for WT, V409I, an V409A, respectively).
source: TUBA1A-V409A cells exhibit a striking increase in microtubule acetylation at the distal axon tip, as well as in the more proximal region of the process (first 10 µm from distal tip: 1.238±0.303, 1.801±0.372, 2.331±0.596 AU; second 10 µm: 2.442±0.416, 3.505±0.556, 3.868±0.702 AU for WT, V409I, an V409A, respectively; Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: There is an increase in the ratio of acetylated to tyrosinated tubulin in the distal 20 µm of the axon in V409I/A cells as compared to WT.
source: Comparing the levels of tyrosinated and acetylated tubulin in each cell, we find an increase in the ratio of acetylated to tyrosinated tubulin in the distal 20 µm of the axon in V409I/A cells as compared to WT (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: There are no significant differences in acetylated tubulin levels in the most distal 10 µm of dendrites between WT and V409I/A cells.
source: In a similar analysis of the most distal 10 µm of dendrites, we find that there are no significant differences in acetylated tubulin levels between WT and V409I/A cells, and thus no difference in the ratio of acetylated to tyrosinated tubulin (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E-F).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E-F.

claim: Some V409I/A cells exhibit increased microtubule acetylation in the dendrite regions that are closer to the soma, which was not observed in WT-expressing cells.
source: However, we observed that some V409I/A cells exhibit increased microtubule acetylation in the dendrite regions that are closer to the soma, which was not observed in WT-expressing cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Cells expressing V409I/A mutants have increased levels of microtubule acetylation as compared to WT.
source: These data suggest that cells expressing V409I/A mutants have increased levels of microtubule acetylation as compared to WT, and V409A cells in particular have abnormally high levels of acetylation at the distal axon tip.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the acetylation data shown in Figure 3.

claim: V409A cells have abnormally high levels of acetylation at the distal axon tip.
source: These data suggest that cells expressing V409I/A mutants have increased levels of microtubule acetylation as compared to WT, and V409A cells in particular have abnormally high levels of acetylation at the distal axon tip.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the acetylation data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The number of growing microtubule events that occur over a 4-min imaging experiment is similar across all genotypes (1846±229, 1746±217, 1785±178 polymerization events/cell/4 min for WT, V409I, V409A, respectively).
source: We find that the number of growing microtubule events that occur over a 4-min imaging experiment is similar across all genotypes (1846±229, 1746±217, 1785±178 polymerization events/cell/4 min for WT, V409I, V409A, respectively; Figure 3F).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Compared to WT, V409A-expressing cells have faster microtubule polymerization rates (5.2±0.1, 6.2±0.1, 6.4±0.1 µm/min for WT, V409I, V409A, respectively).
source: However, compared to WT, V409A-expressing cells have faster microtubule polymerization rates, while V409I cells have an intermediate phenotype between the two (5.2±0.1, 6.2±0.1, 6.4±0.1 µm/min for WT, V409I, V409A, respectively; Figure 3G).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: V409I cells have an intermediate microtubule polymerization rate between WT and V409A.
source: However, compared to WT, V409A-expressing cells have faster microtubule polymerization rates, while V409I cells have an intermediate phenotype between the two (5.2±0.1, 6.2±0.1, 6.4±0.1 µm/min for WT, V409I, V409A, respectively; Figure 3G).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: V409I and V409A cells have slightly but significantly shorter MACF43 comet lifetimes as compared to WT (13.8±0.2, 12.0±0.2, 12.4±0.2 s for WT, V409I, V409A, respectively).
source: In addition, V409I and V409A cells have slightly but significantly shorter MACF43 comet lifetimes as compared to WT (13.8±0.2, 12.0±0.2, 12.4±0.2 s for WT, V409I, V409A, respectively; Figure 3H).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Ectopic expression of TUBA1A-V409I/A mutants alters microtubule dynamics and microtubule acetylation in neurons.
source: We conclude that ectopic expression of TUBA1A-V409I/A mutants alters microtubule dynamics and microtubule acetylation in neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the microtubule dynamics and acetylation data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The α-tubulin V409 residue is highly conserved across eukaryotes.
source: The α-tubulin V409 residue is highly conserved across eukaryotes (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Compared to WT, V410I cells have no significant change in fitness.
source: We find that compared to WT, V410I cells have no significant change in fitness, while V410A cells exhibit a slight fitness defect, as indicated by a 4.4% increase in doubling time (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: V410A cells exhibit a slight fitness defect, as indicated by a 4.4% increase in doubling time.
source: We find that compared to WT, V410I cells have no significant change in fitness, while V410A cells exhibit a slight fitness defect, as indicated by a 4.4% increase in doubling time (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Compared to WT, tub1/tub3-V410A microtubules have significantly faster polymerization rates (1.1±0.1, 1.5±0.1, 1.6±0.1 µm/min for WT, V410I, and V410A, respectively).
source: Compared to WT, we find that tub1/tub3-V410A microtubules have significantly faster polymerization rates, while tub1/tub3-V410I microtubules have intermediate rates between WT and V410A mutants (1.1±0.1, 1.5±0.1, 1.6±0.1 µm/min for WT, V410I, and V410A, respectively; Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: tub1/tub3-V410I microtubules have intermediate polymerization rates between WT and V410A mutants.
source: Compared to WT, we find that tub1/tub3-V410A microtubules have significantly faster polymerization rates, while tub1/tub3-V410I microtubules have intermediate rates between WT and V410A mutants (1.1±0.1, 1.5±0.1, 1.6±0.1 µm/min for WT, V410I, and V410A, respectively; Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: tub1/tub3-V410A microtubules, and to a lesser extent -V410I microtubules, have faster depolymerization rates compared to WT (1.9±0.2, 2.3±0.2, 2.8±0.3 µm/min for WT, V410I, V410A, respectively).
source: Similarly, tub1/tub3-V410A microtubules, and to a lesser extent -V410I microtubules, have faster depolymerization rates compared to WT (1.9±0.2, 2.3±0.2, 2.8±0.3 µm/min for WT, V410I, V410A, respectively; Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: tub1/tub3-V410A microtubules exhibit very few catastrophes compared to WT (1.216±0.105, 0.973±0.111, 0.761±0.106 events/min for WT, V410I, and V410A, respectively).
source: Our data also shows that tub1/tub3-V410A microtubules exhibit very few catastrophes compared to WT, and the tub1/tub3-V410I microtubules again have an intermediate catastrophe frequency (1.216±0.105, 0.973±0.111, 0.761±0.106 events/min for WT, V410I, and V410A, respectively; Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: tub1/tub3-V410I microtubules have an intermediate catastrophe frequency between WT and V410A.
source: Our data also shows that tub1/tub3-V410A microtubules exhibit very few catastrophes compared to WT, and the tub1/tub3-V410I microtubules again have an intermediate catastrophe frequency (1.216±0.105, 0.973±0.111, 0.761±0.106 events/min for WT, V410I, and V410A, respectively; Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: V410I/A microtubules reach longer median lengths than WT microtubules (0.66, 0.68, 0.90 µm for WT, V410I, V410A, respectively).
source: Accordingly, tub1/tub3-V410A mutant microtubules reach longer median lengths than either the tub1/tub3-V410I or WT microtubules (0.66, 0.68, 0.90 µm for WT, V410I, V410A, respectively; Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Astral microtubules in tub1/tub3-V410A mutant cells are retained for a longer time at 4°C than those in WT control cells.
source: Additionally, we find that astral microtubules in tub1/tub3-V410A mutant cells are retained for a longer time at 4°C than those in WT control cells, and tub1/tub3-V410I microtubules have an intermediate phenotype (Figure 4H).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: tub1/tub3-V410I microtubules have an intermediate cold stability phenotype between WT and V410A.
source: Additionally, we find that astral microtubules in tub1/tub3-V410A mutant cells are retained for a longer time at 4°C than those in WT control cells, and tub1/tub3-V410I microtubules have an intermediate phenotype (Figure 4H).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: tub1/tub3-V410A microtubules have the highest dynamicity values (0.443±0.028, 0.507±0.034, 0.563±0.047 subunits/s for WT, V410I, and V410A, respectively).
source: We find that tub1/tub3-V410A microtubules have the highest dynamicity values, while tub1/tub3-V410I microtubules have an intermediate dynamicity between -V410A and WT (0.443±0.028, 0.507±0.034, 0.563±0.047 subunits/s; Figure 4I).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: tub1/tub3-V410I microtubules have an intermediate dynamicity between V410A and WT.
source: We find that tub1/tub3-V410A microtubules have the highest dynamicity values, while tub1/tub3-V410I microtubules have an intermediate dynamicity between -V410A and WT (0.443±0.028, 0.507±0.034, 0.563±0.047 subunits/s; Figure 4I).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: The α-tubulin-V410I/A mutations are sufficient to alter microtubule dynamics in budding yeast.
source: Together, the results of modeling these patient-associated mutations in budding yeast indicate that the α-tubulin-V410I/A mutations are sufficient to alter microtubule dynamics in this system.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the microtubule dynamics data in yeast shown in Figure 4.

claim: The α-tubulin V409 (human) or analogous V410 (yeast) residue resides on the external surface of the tubulin heterodimer near the binding sites of a wide variety of MAPs.
source: The α-tubulin V409 (human) or analogous V410 (yeast) residue resides on the external surface of the tubulin heterodimer near the binding sites of a wide variety of MAPs (Löwe et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim cites Löwe et al., 2001 for the structural location of the residue.

claim: The α-tubulin V410 residue is highlighted as a potential interactor with the TOG2 domain of Crescerin1.
source: In particular, one structural analysis highlights the α-tubulin V410 residue as a potential interactor with the TOG2 domain of Crescerin1 (Das et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim cites Das et al., 2015 for the potential interaction between V410 and TOG2 domain.

claim: The V410 residue appears to reside at the interface between α-tubulin and the TOG1 domain of Stu2.
source: Additionally, the V410 residue appears to reside at the interface between α-tubulin and the TOG1 domain of Stu2 (Figure 5A; Ayaz et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim cites Ayaz et al., 2012 and references Figure 5A showing the structural interface.

claim: tub1/tub3-V410A mutant microtubules have significantly decreased Stu2-3GFP fluorescence intensity at the plus ends compared to WT (3203±333, 1860±165, 1365±143 AU for WT, V410I, and V410A, respectively).
source: We find that tub1/tub3-V410A mutant microtubules have significantly decreased Stu2-3GFP fluorescence intensity at the plus ends compared to WT, while tub1/tub3-V410I microtubules have an intermediate phenotype between the two (3203±333, 1860±165, 1365±143 AU for WT, V410I, and V410A, respectively; Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: tub1/tub3-V410I microtubules have an intermediate Stu2 localization phenotype between WT and V410A.
source: We find that tub1/tub3-V410A mutant microtubules have significantly decreased Stu2-3GFP fluorescence intensity at the plus ends compared to WT, while tub1/tub3-V410I microtubules have an intermediate phenotype between the two (3203±333, 1860±165, 1365±143 AU for WT, V410I, and V410A, respectively; Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Despite having increased microtubule polymerization rates, the tub1/tub3-V410I/A mutant microtubules have less Stu2 at microtubule plus ends.
source: Thus, despite having increased microtubule polymerization rates, the tub1/tub3-V410I/A mutant microtubules have less Stu2 at microtubule plus ends.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Stu2 localization data in Figure 5C and the polymerization rate data in Figure 4D.

claim: V410I, and more significantly V410A, mutant tubulin has decreased affinity for GST-TOG1/2 as compared to WT.
source: Using a low concentration of either WT or V410I/A mutant tubulin in the presence of increasing concentrations of GST-TOG1/2, we find that V410I, and more significantly V410A, mutant tubulin has decreased affinity for GST-TOG1/2 as compared to WT (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The decrease in Stu2 localization at the tub1/tub3-V410I/A microtubule plus ends is a consequence of the decreased affinity of Stu2 TOG1/2 domains for the mutant tubulin.
source: These results indicate that the decrease in Stu2 localization we see at the tub1/tub3-V410I/A microtubule plus ends is a consequence of the decreased affinity of Stu2 TOG1/2 domains for the mutant tubulin.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the binding affinity data in Figure 5D and the localization data in Figure 5C.

claim: After 1.5 hr in 500 µM copper sulfate, Stu2-HA is almost undetectable via western blot.
source: We find that after 1.5 hr in 500 µM copper sulfate (CuSO4), Stu2-HA is almost undetectable via western blot (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Under Stu2 depletion conditions, the proportion of WT cells with visible astral microtubules decreases from 53% to 34% (0.526±0.036, 0.345±0.27 at 0 and 1.5 hr, respectively).
source: Under these conditions, the proportion of WT cells with visible astral microtubules decreases from 53% to 34% (0.526±0.036, 0.345±0.27 at 0 and 1.5 hr, respectively; Figure 5E–F, Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: tub1-V410I and tub1-V410A cells have no significant decrease in proportion of cells that have astral microtubules after 1.5 hr of Stu2 depletion (V410I: 0.537±0.023, 0.516±0.022; V410A: 0.524±0.036, 0.588±0.011 at 0 and 1.5 hr, respectively).
source: In contrast, tub1-V410I and tub1-V410A cells have no significant decrease in proportion of cells that have astral microtubules after 1.5 hr of Stu2 depletion (V410I: 0.537±0.023, 0.516±0.022; V410A: 0.524±0.036, 0.588±0.011 at 0 and 1.5 hr, respectively; Figure 5E–F, Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: V410I and V410A microtubules persist in the absence of Stu2.
source: These data indicate that V410I and V410A microtubules persist in the absence of Stu2, and therefore the mutant tubulins may not require Stu2 polymerase activity to the same extent as WT.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the Stu2 depletion data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: The mutant tubulins may not require Stu2 polymerase activity to the same extent as WT.
source: These data indicate that V410I and V410A microtubules persist in the absence of Stu2, and therefore the mutant tubulins may not require Stu2 polymerase activity to the same extent as WT.
evidence: This is speculation based on the Stu2 depletion data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Purified tub1-V410I microtubules do not have significantly increased polymerization rates as compared to WT at any of the three concentrations tested.
source: In contrast to our results in budding yeast cells, we find that purified tub1-V410I microtubules do not have significantly increased polymerization rates as compared to WT at any of the three concentrations tested (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro dynamics data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: With purified tub1-V410A tubulin, microtubule dynamics could not be observed at concentrations between 0.1 and 1.5 µM.
source: However, with purified tub1-V410A tubulin, we were unable to observe microtubule dynamics at these three concentrations, nor did we observe any at higher concentrations up to 1.5 µM or lower concentrations down to 0.1 µM (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations that are not shown in figures.

claim: At a WT:V410A one-to-one ratio, there is an increase in microtubule polymerization rates at each concentration tested.
source: At this WT:V410A one-to-one ratio, we find an increase in microtubule polymerization rates at each concentration tested (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro dynamics data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The increased microtubule polymerization in WT:V410A mixtures is a synergistic effect of the blend of WT and V410A mutant tubulin.
source: Since the amount of either WT or V410A tubulin that is present in each of these one-to-one mixtures (i.e., 0.25, 0.35, or 0.45 µM) is not sufficient to support microtubule assembly on its own, we conclude that the increased microtubule polymerization is a synergistic effect of the blend of WT and V410A mutant tubulin.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the in vitro dynamics data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: WT/V410A has an ~2-fold increased concentration-dependent polymerization rate as compared to WT and V410I (11.6 compared to 5.8 and 6.5 µm/hr/µM).
source: The slopes of the fitted lines represent the concentration-dependent polymerization rate, and we find that WT/V410A has an ~2-fold increased rate as compared to WT and V410I (11.6 compared to 5.8 and 6.5 µm/hr/µM).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of the fitted lines from the in vitro dynamics data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The critical concentrations for WT, V410I, and WT/V410A are 0.01, 0.02, and 0.02 µM, respectively.
source: The x- and y-intercepts represent the critical concentration and apparent off rate constants, respectively (x-intercepts=0.01, 0.02, and 0.02 µM; y-intercepts=–0.07, –0.13, and –0.18 µm/hr for WT, V410I, and WT/V410A, respectively).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of the fitted lines from the in vitro dynamics data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The apparent off rate constants for WT, V410I, and WT/V410A are –0.07, –0.13, and –0.18 µm/hr, respectively.
source: The x- and y-intercepts represent the critical concentration and apparent off rate constants, respectively (x-intercepts=0.01, 0.02, and 0.02 µM; y-intercepts=–0.07, –0.13, and –0.18 µm/hr for WT, V410I, and WT/V410A, respectively).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of the fitted lines from the in vitro dynamics data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The microtubule depolymerization rates were not different between WT and either the V410I or V410A mutants.
source: In contrast to the increase observed in microtubule polymerization rates, the microtubule depolymerization rates were not different between WT and either the V410I or V410A mutants (Figure 6D).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro dynamics data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: tub1-V410A has significantly increased intrinsic microtubule polymerization as compared to WT.
source: These data indicate that tub1-V410A has significantly increased intrinsic microtubule polymerization as compared to WT.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the in vitro dynamics data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The V409/V410A mutant has the most severe phenotypes across scales, while V409/V410I has more mild effects.
source: Together, our data explain the intrinsic mechanism by which the V409/V410A mutant has the most severe phenotypes across scales, while V409/V410I has more mild effects.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from all the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: TUBA1A is the most highly expressed α-tubulin isotype in post-mitotic neurons in the developing brain.
source: TUBA1A is the most highly expressed α-tubulin isotype in post-mitotic neurons in the developing brain (Buscaglia et al., 2020b; Gloster et al., 1994; Gloster et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim cites Buscaglia et al., 2020b; Gloster et al., 1994; Gloster et al., 1999 for the expression pattern of TUBA1A.

claim: A total of 121 heterozygous, missense mutations have been identified in TUBA1A and are associated with neurodevelopment disorders.
source: To date, a total of 121 heterozygous, missense mutations have been identified in TUBA1A and are associated with neurodevelopment disorders (Hebebrand et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim cites Hebebrand et al., 2019 for the number of TUBA1A mutations.

claim: Some TUBA1A mutants have been identified as loss-of-function mutants that are unable to properly assemble into microtubule polymer.
source: A few of these TUBA1A mutants have been identified as loss-of-function mutants that are unable to properly assemble into microtubule polymer and thus result in an undersupply of tubulin in the cell (Belvindrah et al., 2017; Keays et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim cites Belvindrah et al., 2017; Keays et al., 2007 for loss-of-function TUBA1A mutants.

claim: Other TUBA1A mutants appear to be gain-of-function, as they are capable of microtubule assembly and act dominantly to perturb microtubule function in migrating neurons.
source: However, other TUBA1A mutants appear to be gain-of-function, as they are capable of microtubule assembly and act dominantly to perturb microtubule function in migrating neurons (Aiken et al., 2020; Aiken et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim cites Aiken et al., 2020; Aiken et al., 2019 for gain-of-function TUBA1A mutants.

claim: The patient harboring the V409A mutation exhibited lethal lissencephaly.
source: The patient harboring the V409A mutation exhibited lethal lissencephaly, whereas the patient with the V409I mutation presents with a milder malformation known as pachygyria (Bahi-Buisson et al., 2014; Fallet-Bianco et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim cites Bahi-Buisson et al., 2014; Fallet-Bianco et al., 2014 for the clinical phenotypes of V409A and V409I patients.

claim: The patient with the V409I mutation presents with a milder malformation known as pachygyria.
source: The patient harboring the V409A mutation exhibited lethal lissencephaly, whereas the patient with the V409I mutation presents with a milder malformation known as pachygyria (Bahi-Buisson et al., 2014; Fallet-Bianco et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim cites Bahi-Buisson et al., 2014; Fallet-Bianco et al., 2014 for the clinical phenotypes of V409A and V409I patients.

claim: The V409I/A mutations disrupt XMAP215/Stu2 activity.
source: By modeling the V409I/A mutants at the corresponding residue in budding yeast, V410, we find that the mutants increase microtubule polymerization and depolymerization rates in cells and disrupt XMAP215/Stu2 activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the yeast data shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: The V410A mutation promotes faster microtubule polymerization in reconstitution experiments with purified tubulin, indicating a change in tubulin's intrinsic polymerization activity.
source: Furthermore, the V410A mutation promotes faster microtubule polymerization in reconstitution experiments with purified tubulin, indicating a change in tubulin's intrinsic polymerization activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the in vitro dynamics data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The severity of the V409I and V409A mutations scale from protein activity, to microtubule dynamics in cells, to neuron morphology and migration.
source: Importantly, we find that the severity of the V409I and V409A mutations scale from protein activity, to microtubule dynamics in cells, to neuron morphology and migration.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from all the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The TUBA1A-V409I/A mutations cause brain malformations by subverting dynamic regulation typically conferred by XMAP215.
source: Together, our results suggest that the TUBA1A-V409I/A mutations cause brain malformations by subverting dynamic regulation typically conferred by XMAP215.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from all the data presented in the manuscript.
